filesChanged: packages/envoy/infra/gcp/testdata/dispatch-*.golden (listener-pod, pod, pod-with-azure-federation, pod-with-azure-key, pod-with-broker-and-app, serve, tailnet-pod)
trickyParts: tailnet_service.go and tailnet_service_test.go are shared with INFRA-549 (architect, 02:41Z), which copies them byte for byte; they were committed alone in b1c6c868 and are unchanged since. INFRA-549's implementer has the API.

Approval of a Tailscale Service advertisement is read from the self node's service-host capability in `tailscale status --json` (ipn/ipnlocal/local.go:1565-1573 at v1.104.1), not from the precedent's 'invalid domain' inference.

Liveness and startup probes call /livez with curl and no -f: envoy-dispatch answers 204 with no I/O; the listener has no /livez route and its router answers 404 with no I/O, which still counts as an answer. /healthz (dependency checks) stays readiness only.
Checksum annotations use each Secret's resourceVersion; the TLS Secret carries none and is declared empty with ignoreChanges on data and stringData.
deviations: envoy-infra-v2.6.0 (tag at 819dc283d) released appPriorityClassName after the plan was written, so the rename to priorityClassName now renames a released input. Per plan T10's branch for that case, the CHANGELOG keeps the released entry and records the rename in the Breaking entry; the release is a major bump anyway. Expected release: envoy-infra-v3.0.0.

T9.2 (SetKeepAlivesEnabled(false) at shutdown) is not added: Go's Server.Shutdown already writes every response with Connection: close (net/http server.go doKeepAlives includes shuttingDown). TestShutdownAlreadyClosesKeepAliveConnections records that fact.

Spec items BG-11 and BG-12 (added by the INFRA-63 architect, 04:02Z): proxyCpu/proxyMemory inputs, default 1 CPU / 2Gi (the cloud-sql-proxy v2.26.3 sidecar example); default databaseTier db-custom-4-15360 (max_connections 500 holds 15 pods at 32 connections each); pool.go comment fixed.
Liveness and startup probes use a new /livez endpoint rather than /healthz (simplify pass finding): /healthz on the listener can exceed curl's 8 s on a slow hub and would restart it.
The advertiser container is named advertiser, not cert-order: it advertises, recovers a stuck advertisement, orders the certificate and writes the ready file.

Round 2: besides the tester's red test, the claim gate reads its annotations by the exact key (dots escaped) and drops any ledger entry whose node part holds characters outside A-Za-z0-9./- (the tester's low-severity observation), each with a new test.

Round 2: merged main@origin forward twice (e854d947: conflict in pool.go's sharedPoolSize comment, resolved keeping main's 64 and this change's max_connections bound; 811e6714: conflict in CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Added, both entries kept). main now opens 82 connections per server pod (shared 64, rooms 4, health 1, leases 9, outbox 1, 3 LISTEN), so the default tier db-custom-4-15360 (500 connections) holds 5 replicas rolling (82 x 6 = 492), not 14; the tier is kept and the comments, README and CHANGELOG give those figures.
